explainer: Almost every Royal Wulff line is a variation on Lee Wulff's Triangle Taper: a continuous taper that thickens all the way from the tip to the back of the head, so heavier line is always turning over lighter line. Royal Wulff says this gives delicate delivery, easy roll casts and shooting-head-like distance. Triangle Taper Classic is the original (36-40' taper, offered in four colors) and the brand's best seller.

Signature is Joan Wulff's refinement: a 32-36' front taper plus a short rear taper and a bicolor change behind the head, at standard weight. Signature Plus uses a similar taper built about a half size heavy for faster rods. An archived Triangle Taper Plus page shows the same table, so Signature Plus appears to be that line renamed (our inference). Signature Plus Textured adds a textured coating. Triangle Taper Short (27-29' head, with Bass and Nymph versions) and Ambush (very short 14-31' heads sold by grain weight, for roll casting, single-hand Spey and switch rods) are for tight spots and heavy flies.

Bamboo Special, Long Belly Classic and the Silk line have long bellies or soft heads that suit cane and glass rods. For salt, Bermuda Triangle lines have a braided-mono core for warm water (70°F and above), while Sea Wulff lines are for cold water (75°F and below); both use a 30' 'Triangle Taper Salt' head. Midstream is the budget series ($60-75), with simpler versions of the Classic and Bermuda tapers that have fewer loops and colors.

To choose: go with Classic or Signature for general trout fishing, Signature Plus for fast rods, Short or Ambush for close-range and heavy rigs, Bamboo Special or Long Belly for slow rods, and Bermuda or Sea Wulff by water temperature. Most floating lines carry Royal Wulff's J3 coating. The way buyers should choose is our own synthesis of the maker's descriptions.
